title: String Parsing
prompt:
Write three string parsing functions:

**Requirements:**
1. `parse_csv_line(line)` -- splits a comma-separated line and strips whitespace from each field, returns a list
2. `extract_domain(email)` -- extracts the domain from an email address (part after `@`)
3. `parse_key_value(text, sep="=")` -- parses `"key1=val1,key2=val2"` into a dict `{"key1": "val1", "key2": "val2"}`

**Examples:**
```python
parse_csv_line("a, b, c")                # ["a", "b", "c"]
extract_domain("user@example.com")       # "example.com"
parse_key_value("x=1,y=2")               # {"x": "1", "y": "2"}
```
hints: split(sep, 1) splits only on the first occurrence

solution.py.name: parse_csv_line
solution.py.description: Define a parse_csv_line function that accepts a line parameter

solution.py.name: extract_domain
solution.py.description: Define an extract_domain function that accepts an email parameter

solution.py.name: parse_key_value
solution.py.description: Define a parse_key_value function that accepts text and sep parameters
Use a list comprehension for parsing
solution.py.hint: Use [field.strip() for field in line.split(',')] to split and strip
Use return to produce output from each function
